audit.whatIsWrong: Stored chart is Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Skill / Skill / Wukong / Wukong in both layers. The mirror (audits/top/nautilus__wukong.json) records 'Level 2 Nautilus, Level 3 Skill, Levels 4-5 and 6 Wukong', which is also exactly packet.levelChart, and the whys on this very page say the same: whys[1] 'favoring him', whys[2] 'even out', whys[3] and whys[4] 'favors you'.
audit.why: Ratings are inverse across the mirror and the two directions must not disagree — mirror-fix.js would overwrite these four rows anyway. Four separate signals (mirror, packet chart, this page's own whys, and a 52.57% win rate over 1128 games) all point the same way.
audit.corrected: Flipped rows 1, 2, 3 and 4 in BOTH layers as one atomic paired group: Nautilus at level 2, Skill at level 3, Wukong at 4-5 and at 6. Row 1's rating drops to 4/10; rows 2, 3 and 4 keep ratings that already fit their new side.

audit.whatIsWrong: His spikes are described purely as CC — 'a tank that hits back for very little', 'does almost nothing back'. Titan's Wrath is missing entirely: a shield on a flat 12-second cooldown that, while it holds, makes his attacks burn you and everything around you over time.
audit.why: It changes the all-in maths in both directions — you are burning through a shield AND taking damage-over-time from every auto, which is precisely the trade the page tells you is free.
audit.corrected: Named Titan's Wrath and its 12s cooldown in the first-item spike and the mid prose, without moving any spike 'when' or changing the four-entry count.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three gaps. (a) spikes[1] calls Depth Charge 'a single-target CC ult' — Riot's text says the shockwave rips up the earth as it travels, knocking up enemies along its path, then erupts to knock up and stun the target. It is not single-target. (b) Dredge Line is called 'his only engage', but colliding with TERRAIN pulls Nautilus to the wall — it is also an escape and a repositioning tool, so a baited hook is not always a free window. (c) Riptide never appears anywhere despite being his most frequent spell, a 600-range triple slow on 7s falling to 5s.
audit.why: Each one costs you a fight. Standing beside a teammate who is being ulted still knocks you up; walking him down after a 'wasted' hook can end with him wall-pulling out; and Riptide is the slow that keeps you inside his damage while the shield holds.
audit.corrected: Restated Depth Charge as a path knockup plus a stun on the target, added the terrain pull to the do's, and put Riptide's range and cooldown into the cooldown breakdown. Gave Dredge Line its real 1150 range and 14s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] is headed 'Eat his passive root chain' but its body is unrelated boilerplate: 'Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.'
audit.why: Staggering Blow is the actual mechanic — his FIRST attack on a target roots briefly, which is what turns one hook into a full combo. The reader was given nothing.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the body around Staggering Blow being a first-attack root.

edits.after: Dredge Line reaches 1150 and Staggering Blow roots off his first hit — level 2 is his, so just farm.

notes: The mirror's chart and packet.levelChart agreed exactly, and this page's whys already described that chart, so the four flipped rows are the safest kind of correction — no new judgement, just aligning the stored sides with three sources that already agreed. The Depth Charge 'single-target' claim is the most dangerous line that was on the page: a Wukong who believes it will stand next to the ulted teammate and eat the path knockup. Not asserted because the data cannot settle it: whether Cyclone's knockup can interrupt Dredge Line's pull mid-flight, whether Depth Charge's stun is QSS-able or shortened by tenacity, and whether the clone can eat the hook. The mirror also noted the content prose here is first-person in places — mid and late still read fine in second person after this pass, but the untouched early/late lines are worth a human look.
